meta.title: General American vowels (chart-matched)
meta.note: Inventory + examples match the provided screenshot as closely as possible from the image. Audio is expected at site/audio/phonemes/<key>.mp3 and site/audio/words/<slug>.mp3

articulatory.tongue: High Front: Tongue blade arches high toward the hard palate near the alveolar ridge.
articulatory.jaw: High / nearly closed (narrow gap between incisors).
articulatory.lips: Unrounded, spread into a slight smile.
articulatory.cue: Sides of the tongue press firmly against upper molars. Pharynx and throat cavity stay wide and relaxed.

articulatory.tongue: High-Mid Front (Lax): Tongue body is slightly lower and more central than /i/, with relaxed muscle tension.
articulatory.jaw: Slightly more open than /i/ (relaxed jaw drop).
articulatory.lips: Unrounded and relaxed.
articulatory.cue: Relax the tongue and jaw from the /i/ position. Sound feels centered in the high-front mouth.

articulatory.tongue: Starts in high-front /ɪ/ position, then tongue body retracts and curls/bunches into the rhotic pocket.
articulatory.lips: Unrounded, transitioning to slight lip flare.
articulatory.cue: Tongue sweeps from high-front lax position backward toward the palate for the /r/ finish.

articulatory.tongue: Diphthong Glide: Starts at mid-front /e/ and moves smoothly upward toward high-front /ɪ/.
articulatory.jaw: Starts mid-open and raises upward as the glide finishes.
articulatory.lips: Unrounded, spreading progressively wider.
articulatory.cue: Feel the upward jaw movement and tongue blade gliding upward toward the hard palate.

articulatory.tongue: Mid Front: Tongue body sits at half-height in the front oral cavity, below the hard palate.
articulatory.jaw: Mid-open (approx. one finger width between front teeth).
articulatory.lips: Unrounded and neutral.
articulatory.cue: Tongue blade is arched mid-level; sides lightly contact upper rear teeth.

articulatory.tongue: Starts at mid-front /ɛ/ and glides directly into the bunched or retroflex rhotic /r/.
articulatory.jaw: Mid-open, closing slightly during the glide.
articulatory.lips: Neutral, transitioning to slight lip protrusion.
articulatory.cue: Hold the open /ɛ/ position, then bunch the back of the tongue or curl the tip for the rhotic resonance.

articulatory.tongue: Stressed Rhotic: Tongue body bunches high in the central palate with tip curled (retroflex) or bunched back.
articulatory.jaw: Mid-high opening with active muscular tension.
articulatory.lips: Moderately rounded with slight flaring of lips.
articulatory.cue: Dual constriction in palate and pharynx creates the strong General American /r/ acoustic resonance.

articulatory.tongue: Unstressed Rhotic (schwa+r): Same bunched or retroflex posture as /ɝ/, but quick, unstressed, and light.
articulatory.lips: Neutral to slightly rounded.
articulatory.cue: Unstressed syllables (water, actor). Tongue touches the rhotic pocket lightly and briefly.

articulatory.tongue: Low-Front/Central Anchor [a]: Lowest point of the front-to-back arc, starting anchor for /aɪ/ and /aʊ/.
articulatory.lips: Unrounded and neutral.
articulatory.cue: Open base anchor sound for General American open diphthongs.

articulatory.tongue: High Back: Tongue dorsum arches high toward the velum (soft palate) at the back of the mouth.
articulatory.lips: Tightly rounded and protruded into a small circle.
articulatory.cue: Tongue pulls far back toward the soft palate/uvula while lips make a tight circular tube.

articulatory.tongue: High-Mid Back (Lax): Tongue dorsum is slightly lower and less retracted than /u/, muscles relaxed.
articulatory.lips: Loosely rounded, not tightly pursed.
articulatory.cue: Relax lips and tongue from the /u/ position (foot, look, put).

articulatory.tongue: Starts in high-back lax /ʊ/ position and transitions into central rhotic bunched /r/.
articulatory.lips: Rounded, maintaining active lip engagement throughout.
articulatory.cue: Glides from rounded back cavity inward to the central rhotic constriction (tour, cure).

articulatory.tongue: Mid Central / Back-Central (Stressed): Tongue body sits at relaxed mid height, slightly back of center.
articulatory.lips: Completely unrounded and neutral.
articulatory.cue: Short, punchy stressed vowel in the center-back of the mouth (sun, cup, blood).

articulatory.tongue: Mid Central (Schwa): Neutral vocal tract; tongue rests in the exact center of the mouth without tension.
articulatory.lips: Completely relaxed, neutral.
articulatory.cue: The lazy default resting posture of English; zero muscular strain (ago, the).

articulatory.tongue: Diphthong Glide: Starts at mid-back /o/ and glides upward and backward toward /ʊ/.
articulatory.lips: Rounded at start, becoming tighter and more protruded as the sound finishes.
articulatory.cue: Feel both jaw closing and lip circle shrinking as you say 'no', 'go', 'boat'.

articulatory.tongue: Mid Back (Open-Mid): Tongue body pulled back toward the posterior pharyngeal wall and lower velum.
articulatory.lips: Moderately rounded (oval aperture).
articulatory.cue: Acoustic resonance feels deep in the throat/pharynx with distinct lip rounding (law, saw, caught).

articulatory.tongue: Starts with rounded mid-back /ɔ/ and glides smoothly into the central rhotic bunched /r/.
articulatory.lips: Maintains rounding through to the rhotic finish.
articulatory.cue: Prominent General American vowel in words like 'warm', 'door', 'form'.

articulatory.tongue: Low Front: Tongue blade lies low and forward behind the lower teeth; pharynx narrows slightly.
articulatory.lips: Unrounded, corners pulled back slightly.
articulatory.cue: Tongue tip touches lower front teeth while tongue body stays low and flat in front (cat, hat, ash).

articulatory.tongue: Diphthong Glide: Starts low in front/center /a/ and travels diagonally upward to high-back /ʊ/.
articulatory.jaw: Drops wide open on start, then closes upward noticeably.
articulatory.lips: Starts completely unrounded/open, finishes tightly rounded.
articulatory.cue: Dramatic full-mouth articulatory travel: from wide open flat tongue to high rounded back (cow, loud).

articulatory.tongue: Triphthong Glide: Starts low /a/, sweeps through back /ʊ/, and finishes in central rhotic /r/.
articulatory.jaw: Wide open at start, closes upward.
articulatory.lips: Starts neutral, rounds, then relaxes into rhotic shape.
articulatory.cue: Multi-stage articulatory movement heard in words like 'hour', 'sour'.

articulatory.tongue: Diphthong Glide: Starts low in front/center /a/ and glides upward toward high-front /ɪ/.
articulatory.jaw: Starts wide open and closes upward toward the upper incisors.
articulatory.lips: Starts neutral/unrounded, widens into a smile.
articulatory.cue: Tongue sweeps up the front of the mouth from lowest floor to hard palate (sky, fly, time).

articulatory.tongue: Triphthong Glide: Starts low /a/, glides toward front /ɪ/, then sweeps to central rhotic /r/.
articulatory.lips: Unrounded, transitions to slight rhotic posture.
articulatory.cue: Triple transition heard in 'wire', 'fire', 'tire'.

articulatory.tongue: Low Back: Tongue body pulled all the way back and down into the lower pharynx / throat.
articulatory.jaw: Maximum low opening / wide dropped jaw.
articulatory.lips: Completely unrounded, neutral opening.
articulatory.cue: Doctor's visit 'say Ah': tongue flat and retracted low, opening the entire oral cavity (top, hot, cot).

articulatory.tongue: Starts at low back /ɑ/ and glides into bunched or retroflex rhotic /r/.
articulatory.jaw: Wide open at start, closes slightly.
articulatory.lips: Neutral unrounded at start, slight flare for /r/ finish.
articulatory.cue: Classic 'car', 'hard', 'arm' vowel in General American.
